authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 3865.1 gives Prakrit khāaï/khāi, Hindi khānā, Marwari khābo and Gujarati khāvũ. These selected khā-/khā-o imperatives contain the eating stem and an ordinary imperative ending; compound completives are excluded.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6141 derives regional de- from Middle Indo-Aryan dēti/dēi, remodeled with imperative dēhi and the ‘take’ paradigm. The bare imperative belongs here; diyā and doubled de-de are excluded from this proposal.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 1200 specifically compares Prakrit āvaï ‘comes’, Hindi ānā with stem āw-, Old Marwari āvaï and Gujarati āvvũ under āpayati. The selected come-imperatives belong here, while āyo past forms and ā-ja compounds require separate analysis.
